## Overview Preserve leading whitespace when the Rust frontend decodes SentencePiece/Metaspace tokens individually for logprobs. Related issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44319 Python reference: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48674 ## Claims - Prevents distinct tokens such as `▁the` and `the` from both being reported as `"the"`. - Prevents `top_logprobs` entries from overwriting each other when decoded token strings are used as map keys. - Keeps completion `text_offset` values aligned with the generated text. - Supports direct Metaspace pre-tokenizers and Metaspace inside a `Sequence`. - Preserves existing behavior for non-Metaspace tokenizers and normal sequence decoding. ## Validation ```bash cargo nextest run -p vllm-tokenizer -p vllm-text -p vllm-server --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast cargo fmt --all -- --check cargo clippy -p vllm-tokenizer -p vllm-text -p vllm-server --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings ``` ## Details Metaspace represents word-boundary whitespace inside raw vocabulary pieces, for example ▁the. When such a token is decoded in isolation, the decoder treats it as the beginning of a string and may remove the leading space. Consequently, both ▁the and the can decode to "the". Completion logprobs use decoded token strings as map keys. Identical decoded strings cause one candidate to overwrite another. The missing space also makes subsequent character offsets too small. The tokenizer now records the configured Metaspace replacement character during construction. A dedicated per-token decoding method compares the raw vocabulary piece with the decoded string and restores only missing leading spaces. Other tokenizer implementations retain the existing decoding behavior through the default method. The logprobs path uses this per-token method, while normal sequence and incremental decoding remain unchanged. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
